title: WPSS/1872/2005 of DALBIR SINGH NEGI Vs STATE and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARANCHAL AT
NAINITAL.
Writ Petition No. 1872 (S/S) of 2005
Dalbir Singh Negi, son of Sri Kundan Singh Negi, resident
of village - Saloor Dungra, Post Office - Saloor Dangra,
District - Chamoli, presently posted as Assistant Teacher LT
Grade English, Painkanda Uchhatar Madhyamik Vidyalaya,
Saloor Dungra, Block - Joshi Math, District - Chamoli.
........Petitioner.
Versus.
1. State of Uttaranchal through Secretary, Secondary
Education, Government of Uttaranchal, Dehradun.
2. Director, Education Secondary and Intermediate,
Education, Government of Uttaranchal, Dehradun.
3. District Education Officer, Chamoli.
4. The Committee of Management Painkanda
Uchhatar Madhyamik Vidyalaya through its Manager
Sri M.N. Bainjwal.
5. Principal, Painkanda Uchhatar Madhyamik
Vidyalaya, Saloor Dungra, Block - Joshi Math, District
- Chamoli.
...........Respondents.
Hon'ble M.M. Ghildiyal, J.:
Heard Sri Pankaj Purohit, leaned counsel for the
petitioner and learned standing counsel for respondent no.
1 to 3.
By means of this writ petition, the petitioner has
challenged the advertisement no. 1 of 2005 dated 24.10.2005
published on 21.11.2005 in the daily newspaper "Amar
Ujala" for the post of Assistant Teachers in Painkanda
Uchhatar Madhyamik Vidyalaya, Saloor Dunga, Block -
Joshi Math, District - Chamoli.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that
the school was opened for the first time in the year 1994
and the petitioner was appointed as Assistant Teacher
(English) by the Committee of Management vide its order
dated 06.07.1994. In the year 1997, the Institute was
accorded recognition and was brought under grand-in-aid
vide order dated 02.09.1997. After the recognition was
granted to the Institution and the Institution was brought
under grant-in-aid. The petitioner was again appointed on
the post of Assistant Teacher LT Grade English by
respondent no. 4 vide order dated 04.11.1997 and since then
he is continuing in the said Institution. However,
respondent no. 4 has published the advertisement for the
post of Assistant Teachers.
The submission of the petitioner is that he is entitled
to be regularized on the post of Assistant Teacher and the
Committee of Management should not have any right to fill
up the post on which he is working.
From the appointment letter issued by the Committee
of Management, it appears that petitioner was not
appointed on regular basis and he was appointed as a part
time teacher on a consolidated salary of Rs. 1800/- per
month. In view of the appointment letter dated 04.11.1997
petitioner does not have any right to be regularized on the
post. Petitioner has already applied for the appointment in
pursuance to the advertisement.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that
there is no mention of preference for those persons who are
already working in the Institution and as such, respondents

be directed to give preference to the petitioner as he has
been teaching in the Institution since 1997.
It is for the Selection Committee or Institution to
consider the case of the petitioner and to decide whether
preference should be given to the petitioner or not? This
court cannot direct the Institution / Selection Committee to
give preference to the petitioner. However, the Selection
Committee or the Institution can consider the case of the
petitioner for making appointment on the post of Assistant
Teacher considering the fact that petitioner has already
worked in the Institution for so many years.
With this direction the writ petition is finally disposed
of. No order as to costs.
(M.M. Ghildiyal, J.)
December 16, 2005
SKSharma
